definitions.explanation: Visiting a place in advance to check its suitability before a main event. Common when choosing venues for weddings, parties, or trips.

examples.japanese: {会場|かいじょう}の{下見|したみ}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to preview the venue.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}{前|まえ}にホテルを{下見|したみ}しておきたい。
examples.english: I want to check out the hotel before the trip.

examples.japanese: {結婚式|けっこんしき}の{会場|かいじょう}を{決|き}めるため、{三|みっ}つの{式場|しきじょう}を{下見|したみ}した。
examples.english: To choose a wedding venue, I previewed three ceremony halls.

notes:
The verb form {下見|したみ}する means "to make a preliminary visit" or "to scout out." Very commonly used when planning weddings, events, or travel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {会場|かいじょう}の{下見|したみ} (venue preview)
- {下見|したみ}に{行|い}く (to go on a preliminary visit)
- {式場|しきじょう}の{下見|したみ} (ceremony hall preview)
- {物件|ぶっけん}の{下見|したみ} (property viewing)

USAGE NOTE: {下見|したみ} implies checking something out before committing. It is not used for casual browsing — it suggests a specific purpose.
